pipeline.description:
The ``pipeline`` section.

``max_workers`` is how many independent steps may run at once.
``env_file`` is a ``.env`` file, relative to the folder you run from, whose
variables are loaded before anything else so ``${env:NAME}`` references
and Azure sign-in can use them. Variables already set in the environment
keep their values.
pipeline.title: PipelineMeta

anyOf.description: Files of shared connections, relative to the folder you run from.

connections.description: Named connections: where data lives and how to sign in.

then.description:
Files in an Azure Blob Storage container.

With account, sign-in uses DefaultAzureCredential: your
az login locally, a managed identity in Azure, or service principal
environment variables. With connection_string, that string is used.
Step paths are relative to prefix within the container.
then.title: AzureBlobConfig
then.markdownDescription:
Files in an Azure Blob Storage container.

With `account`, sign-in uses `DefaultAzureCredential`: your
`az login` locally, a managed identity in Azure, or service principal
environment variables. With `connection_string`, that string is used.
Step paths are relative to `prefix` within the container.

then.description:
Azure SQL Database or SQL Server.

With server and database, sign-in uses an Entra ID token from
DefaultAzureCredential: your az login locally, a managed identity
in Azure. A fresh token is fetched for every new database connection, so
long runs aren't cut off when a token expires. With
connection_string, that ODBC connection string is used as it is.

Writes use pyodbc's fast_executemany.
then.title: AzureSQLConfig
then.markdownDescription:
Azure SQL Database or SQL Server.

With `server` and `database`, sign-in uses an Entra ID token from
`DefaultAzureCredential`: your `az login` locally, a managed identity
in Azure. A fresh token is fetched for every new database connection, so
long runs aren't cut off when a token expires. With
`connection_string`, that ODBC connection string is used as it is.

Writes use pyodbc's `fast_executemany`.

then.description:
Files on the local filesystem.

Step paths are relative to root, and a relative root is relative
to the folder you run from. Parent folders are
created when writing, and a file is written under a temporary name and
only then put in place, so a failed write leaves the old file untouched.
then.title: LocalConfig
then.markdownDescription:
Files on the local filesystem.

Step paths are relative to `root`, and a relative `root` is relative
to the folder you run from. Parent folders are
created when writing, and a file is written under a temporary name and
only then put in place, so a failed write leaves the old file untouched.

then.description:
Files in a SharePoint document library.

Signs in with DefaultAzureCredential, so the identity needs Graph
permission to the site's files (for example Sites.Selected or
Sites.ReadWrite.All for a service principal). Step paths are
relative to folder in library. Wildcards are allowed in file
names, not in folder names. Uploads are limited to 250 MB.
then.title: SharePointConfig
then.markdownDescription:
Files in a SharePoint document library.

Signs in with `DefaultAzureCredential`, so the identity needs Graph
permission to the site's files (for example `Sites.Selected` or
`Sites.ReadWrite.All` for a service principal). Step paths are
relative to `folder` in `library`. Wildcards are allowed in file
names, not in folder names. Uploads are limited to 250 MB.

then.description:
Any database SQLAlchemy supports, given a database URL.

A relative SQLite path is relative to the folder you run from, and
the folder for a new SQLite file is created.
then.title: SQLConfig
then.markdownDescription:

then.description:
Applies operations in order, each to the last one's result.

The chain starts from the data input, or from the table the first
operation names (join: {left: ..., right: ...}). The operations are
checked when the pipeline loads.

operations.description: The operations, applied in order, each to the last result.

aggregate.description:
Group rows by by and aggregate each column with the named function.

columns maps a column to sum, mean, count, min,
max or any other pandas aggregation.
aggregate.markdownDescription:
Group rows by `by` and aggregate each column with the named function.

`columns` maps a column to `sum`, `mean`, `count`, `min`,
`max` or any other pandas aggregation.

cast.description:
Convert columns to a type, written as column: type.

Types are int, float, str, bool and datetime, or any
pandas type name, such as category or int32.
cast.markdownDescription:
Convert columns to a type, written as `column: type`.

Types are `int`, `float`, `str`, `bool` and `datetime`, or any
pandas type name, such as `category` or `int32`.

check.description:
Check the table and pass it on unchanged, or fail with every problem found.

columns must exist; not_null columns have no missing values;
unique columns, together, identify each row; accepted maps a
column to its allowed values; min_rows and max_rows bound the
row count. With warn, problems are logged as a warning instead.
check.markdownDescription:
Check the table and pass it on unchanged, or fail with every problem found.

`columns` must exist; `not_null` columns have no missing values;
`unique` columns, together, identify each row; `accepted` maps a
column to its allowed values; `min_rows` and `max_rows` bound the
row count. With `warn`, problems are logged as a warning instead.

dedupe.description:
Drop repeated rows: the same in subset, or in every column.

keep says which of the repeats stays: the first or the last.
dedupe.markdownDescription:
Drop repeated rows: the same in `subset`, or in every column.

`keep` says which of the repeats stays: the `first` or the `last`.

derive.description:
Add or replace columns, written as column: expression.

Expressions are arithmetic and comparisons on other columns, as for
DataFrame.eval: total: price * quantity. Each can use the ones
before it.
derive.markdownDescription:
Add or replace columns, written as `column: expression`.

Expressions are arithmetic and comparisons on other columns, as for
`DataFrame.eval`: `total: price * quantity`. Each can use the ones
before it.

drop_nulls.description: Drop rows with a missing value in any of subset, or in any column.
drop_nulls.markdownDescription: Drop rows with a missing value in any of `subset`, or in any column.

fill_nulls.description: Fill missing values, written as column: value.
fill_nulls.markdownDescription: Fill missing values, written as `column: value`.

filter.description:
Keep the rows matching expression, such as amount > 100.

Written as for DataFrame.query: and, or, ==, in, and
backticks around column names with spaces.
filter.markdownDescription:
Keep the rows matching `expression`, such as `amount > 100`.

Written as for `DataFrame.query`: `and`, `or`, `==`, `in`, and
backticks around column names with spaces.

flatten.description:
Turn documents into a table, with pandas.json_normalize.

data is a document or a list of them. Nested objects become dotted
columns (user.id); record_path takes the rows from a list inside
each document, meta copies document fields onto each row (nested
ones as a list, such as [source, system]), max_level limits how
deep objects are flattened, and sep joins the names of nested ones.
flatten.markdownDescription:
Turn documents into a table, with `pandas.json_normalize`.

`data` is a document or a list of them. Nested objects become dotted
columns (`user.id`); `record_path` takes the rows from a list inside
each document, `meta` copies document fields onto each row (nested
ones as a list, such as `[source, system]`), `max_level` limits how
deep objects are flattened, and `sep` joins the names of nested ones.

right.description: The name of one of the step's inputs.

left.description: The name of one of the step's inputs.

join.description:
Join the left table with the right one on shared columns.

right names another of the step's inputs. left names one too
when the join comes first in a transform; later, the left side is the
result so far. Match on on, or on left_on and right_on when
the columns are named differently. how is inner, left,
right or outer. suffixes tell apart other columns both sides
have (default [_x, _y]). validate fails the join unless keys
match as expected, such as many_to_one.
join.markdownDescription:
Join the `left` table with the `right` one on shared columns.

`right` names another of the step's inputs. `left` names one too
when the join comes first in a transform; later, the left side is the
result so far. Match on `on`, or on `left_on` and `right_on` when
the columns are named differently. `how` is `inner`, `left`,
`right` or `outer`. `suffixes` tell apart other columns both sides
have (default `[_x, _y]`). `validate` fails the join unless keys
match as expected, such as `many_to_one`.

python.description:
Call callable (module:function) with the data and args.

The function gets the current table first, then args by name, and
returns the table the next operation works on.
python.markdownDescription:
Call `callable` (`module:function`) with the data and `args`.

The function gets the current table first, then `args` by name, and
returns the table the next operation works on.

rename.description: Rename columns, written as old name: new name.
rename.markdownDescription: Rename columns, written as `old name: new name`.

select.description: Keep only columns, in that order.

sort.description: Sort rows by one or more columns; ascending can be one per column.
sort.markdownDescription: Sort rows by one or more columns; `ascending` can be one per column.

SQLPartition.description:
Split a read into ranges of a whole-number column, read at the same time.

Reading a ``table``, set ``column``: its range comes from the column's
MIN and MAX unless ``lower`` and ``upper`` are set, and rows where it's
NULL are read too. Reading a query, put ``:partition_start`` and
``:partition_end`` where the range belongs (for example ``WHERE
order_id BETWEEN :partition_start AND :partition_end``) and set
``lower`` and ``upper``.
SQLPartition.title: SQLPartition
